title: The messenger and the uniform
header_line: My analysis of one book on authority and personal brand. Not a summary of the book. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the author or publisher.

lines.text: Are you the messenger or the message?

A student said: the book sets up that we want to be an authority in our space, to be the messenger and not necessarily the message. I like that they address social media, because it is a way to build authority in this age.

I said that reading these books empowers us because we learn words that carry deep concepts. I said that the two concepts I heard most from the author when we met were mission-driven authority and being a servant leader.

I said that the company is every person and the roles and responsibilities they play, and that in each contact there is a standard of how they speak and carry themselves. I said that is why people wear uniforms: a uniform changes your mindset to I am in that role.
I said that without a uniform you are more likely to fall out of the role, and that our lives are filled with uniforms and roles.
What is your uniform, even if it is not cloth?

exercise.title: Five minutes
steps: Write what makes you its messenger.
Write the role you play when you are at your best.
Write how you will keep to the standard when no one is looking.

check.q: What did a student say we want to be?
What did I say a uniform changes?
What two concepts did I say the author talks about most?

recap: Be the messenger. Play your role to its standard.
